subject: Post-demo: BluePeak integration summary & technical next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@bluepeak.ai>; Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@bluepeak.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: BluePeak integration summary & technical next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our demo and the most important things we heard from you, plus proposed next steps. I wanted to make sure we captured the pain, the success criteria, and the technical asks so everyone is aligned.

Pain points / goals you shared:
- Low-quality search results in the analytics UI: noisy matches and overloaded signals.
- Need for a reranking layer that is fast (p95 < 150ms on query) and cost-predictable.
- Desire to add structured output for entity extraction in the recommendation pipeline so downstream rules can run deterministically.
- Data residency constraints: logs and user data must stay in US-east region and meet your retention policy.

Product-fit notes we covered:
- Embeddings + sparse-first rerank: run an approximate nearest-neighbors step client-side (your vector DB) then call Redwood for a rerank/score using streaming generation for top-K candidates.
- Streaming + function calling: we demoed streaming score deltas and a function-call pattern to return a JSON structure with confidence, tags, and canonical entity ids.
- SDK changes: minimal — a small helper wrapper in your query path to batch top-K candidates and invoke the /rerank endpoint with streaming enabled.

Technical asks we captured:
1) Latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for rerank-only path; bulk scoring can be higher.
2) Throughput: expected steady 120 qps, burst to 400 qps during reports.
3) Data residency & logs: audit log export to your S3 + option for VPC Private deployment for the proof-of-concept.
4) Output schema: strict JSON object with fields {score, label, entity_id, tags[]} — we'll provide a sample schema.

Attachments: I attached a quick integration notes doc, a diagram of the proposed data flow, and a draft MVP scope matrix.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical kickoff (30–45m): Tue 2026-12-10 10:00am ET — engineering + infra folks (we can send a calendar invite).
- Trial plan: 2-week sandbox on Redwood Dedicated with a scoped token for test data; we’ll provide a benchmark script.
- Follow-up: Vivek and Aditya to send pricing options and a short SOW for the POC.

Question for you: can you confirm whether BluePeak prefers a Hosted sandbox with VPC egress or a short-lived Dedicated pool for the POC? That will determine the onboarding steps and the SLA commitments.

Thanks — very excited about the fit.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0214

---
Attachments: redwood_sdk_integration_notes.pdf (summary), bp_data_flow_v1.drawio (diagram), mvp_scope_matrix.xlsx (matrix)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@bluepeak.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@bluepeak.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BluePeak integration summary & technical next steps

Thanks Sofia — this is great and captures the discussion. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Throughput numbers: the 120 qps steady is per-region (we're thinking US-east traffic only for now). The 400 qps burst is global during report generation windows (but we can stagger).
- Latency: the 150ms p95 target is critical for interactive user sessions; for background batch rerank of historical results we can accept longer windows.
- Output schema: the example looks good but we need the entity_id to map to our canonical ids (we'll provide a mapping).
- Security: we'll need a short SOC2 questionnaire answered and a list of your sub-processors before we share sample data.

Regarding the POC: we'd prefer a Dedicated sandbox if the timeline is short and we can avoid data movement. If Redwood can guarantee the audit log export and the VPC egress configuration for the Dedicated pool, we'd take that. Otherwise a hosted sandbox with VPC egress will work for the first week.

I'll loop in our infra lead on the kickoff invite once we confirm the date.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | BluePeak Analytics
alex.johnson@bluepeak.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T19:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BluePeak integration summary & technical next steps

Nice recap — two internal notes: 
1) For Dedicated sandbox: operations can provision a small 4xA10 pool in us-east with VPC egress for logs. We should be able to disable long-term retention and enable S3 export of request logs within 48h of kickoff. I'll confirm with infra tomorrow.
2) Pricing: we can do a timeboxed POC discount (40% off list) with a capped token budget for the 2-week trial. Aditya, please draft the POC SOW + pricing options and include a billing/commit clause in case they convert.

Also recommend we prepare a short benchmarking script (Python) that:
- uploads a sample dataset to their vector DB (we will provide vectorizer examples),
- runs top-K fetch + Redwood rerank for 1k synthetic queries,
- reports p50/p95/p99 and token cost.

Monica — can you prep the SOC2 questionnaire and the sub-processor list to attach to the kickoff packet?

Vivek
VP, Solutions | Redwood Inference

- We'll provision a Dedicated sandbox in us-east for the POC unless you instruct otherwise; operations will confirm the pool sizing and VPC egress by EOD 2026-12-07.
- Aditya will send the POC SOW + 40% POC pricing and a capped token budget by tomorrow.
- Monica will attach SOC2 questionnaire and the sub-processor list to the kickoff packet.
- Technical kickoff: tentatively Tue 2026-12-10 10:00am ET — I'll follow up with a calendar invite and a short agenda (30m).

If BluePeak can share an initial mapping file and a small sample dataset (anonymized) ahead of the call that would help us shorten the benchmark turnaround.

Thanks again — looking forward to the POC.

Best,
